messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty escalation fired for service "hosted-inference" (pd_incident: PD123456). Symptom: sustained 502 spikes, 10% error rate > threshold for 3m. Primary on-call: alice-engineering (no ack). Escalated to secondary: tina-oncall. Policy: 2-minute wait -> manager dave-manager if unacked.

Tina-oncall: got the page, investigating now. seeing a spike in 502s from model-runtime replicas in us-east-1c. jumping in.

ben-sre: I can help. are the 502s originating at the edge LB or inside the inference pods?

Tina-oncall: appears inside the runtime. tailing logs shows repeated stream write failures on some pods. attaching snippet.

Tina-oncall: ```bash
# tail from runtime container (shortened)
kubectl -n inference logs -l app=model-serve -c runtime --tail=200 | grep "stream write error"
2026-03-15T11:02:14Z runtime-0 stream write error: broken pipe
2026-03-15T11:02:15Z runtime-3 stream write error: broken pipe
```

carla-support: copying from customer slack — several customers report timeouts for /v1/generate since 11:02 UTC. at least 8 customers affected with elevated latencies >30s.

ben-sre: quick mitigation plan: scale up model-serving replicas and restart the oldest pods to clear stuck KV/cache state. Tina, can you run: 
```bash
kubectl scale deployment/model-serve --replicas=10 -n inference
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-serve -n inference
```

Tina-oncall: scaling now, running rollout restart. will post updates as pods become ready. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

incident-bot: PagerDuty update: 2m elapsed since escalation. No ack from alice-engineering. Manager escalation to dave-manager triggered.

dave-manager: pinged mobile — on my way if needed. before we go to exec, can we confirm customer impact / scope?

carla-support: confirmed impact: 8 customers with >30s latencies, 3 with transient 502s. no data loss reported. drafting a short status message for customers now.

ben-sre: rollout shows new pods passing readiness probes. error rate down from ~12% to ~2% in the last 90s. maybe the stuck KV windows were cleared during restart.

Tina-oncall: new pods are ready and receiving traffic. I've restarted the three oldest replicas. continuing to monitor for 10m.

Alice-engineering: acked the incident (late — sorry, was on another page). back now and digging into root cause. initial hypothesis: KV cache eviction race + continuous batching under high concurrency. will own the postmortem.

carla-support: publishing customer update draft to #status for review: "We experienced intermittent 502s affecting generate endpoints. We applied scaling and rolling restarts to affected runtime pods which mitigated the issue. No customer data was lost. We will follow up with a postmortem and long-term fix."

ben-sre: recommendation: keep incident open until metrics stable for 10m and then close. create follow-up ticket to investigate KV cache eviction and add guardrails.

Tina-oncall: handing off to Alice for root cause and postmortem. I'll stay on watch for 15m and then drop out if stable.

incident-bot: Condition cleared: error rate <1% for 5m. PagerDuty incident PD123456 auto-resolve scheduled. :white_check_mark:

carla-support: will send customer follow-up in 30m and include mitigation timeline.

Alice-engineering: thanks everyone — will open a Github issue with replication steps, logs, and proposed fixes (KV eviction backoff + safer cache drains).
